title: SMC High Probability Inducement & Engineered Liquidity

multiple_inducements.llm_summary: A swing can have one or more inducement levels. Every valid pullback within a swing is an inducement. Sometimes a swing has a single inducement (one pullback), sometimes two, and sometimes more than two. When there are multiple inducements, the question becomes: which inducement level should be used for planning buy/sell setups? There are two types: Minor Inducement (small/short pullback) and Major Inducement (deep pullback). The key distinction is that for structure mapping, the FIRST inducement is always used. But for planning buy/sell entries, the MAJOR (high probability) inducement should be considered.
key_rules: A swing can have 1, 2, or more inducement levels
Every valid pullback within a swing = inducement
Two types: Minor Inducement (small pullback) and Major Inducement (deep pullback)
For STRUCTURE MAPPING: always use the FIRST inducement level
For BUY/SELL SETUP PLANNING: use the MAJOR (high probability) inducement
These are different use cases — mapping vs entry planning

high_probability_inducement.llm_summary: High Probability Inducement is the MAJOR inducement within a swing — the deepest pullback compared to others. When multiple inducements exist, the major one (deepest) is the high probability inducement. 80-85% of the time, market trades the major inducement before moving in its major direction. Three rules determine high probability inducement: (1) If there's only one inducement, that IS the high probability inducement. (2) If there are multiple inducements of different sizes, the MAJOR (deepest) one is high probability. (3) If all inducements are the SAME SIZE, the FIRST one is high probability. The size of inducement correlates with the size of market's subsequent move: minor inducement → minor reaction (small move), major inducement → major reaction (large move). When planning buy/sell entries, find the major inducement and look for order blocks BELOW it — this gives 80-85% high probability setup.
key_rules: High Probability Inducement = MAJOR inducement (deepest pullback in the swing)
80-85% chance market trades major inducement before continuing in major direction
Rule 1: Single inducement → it IS the high probability inducement
Rule 2: Multiple different sizes → MAJOR (deepest) is high probability
Rule 3: All same size → FIRST one is high probability
Minor inducement → minor market reaction (small move)
Major inducement → major market reaction (large move)
For entry planning: find major inducement → look for order block below it → 80-85% setup
Structure mapping still uses first inducement regardless of size

engineered_liquidity_definition.llm_summary: Engineered Liquidity (ENG LIQ) is an area where Smart Money designs traps for retail Support and Resistance based traders. Market creates equal highs, equal lows, double tops, double bottoms, and trendline patterns that retail traders interpret as support/resistance or chart patterns (bull flag, bearish flag, channels). These are NOT real support/resistance — they are liquidity traps engineered by Smart Money. When price creates multiple lows at the same level, retail traders see 'strong support' and place buy orders. When price creates equal highs, retail sees 'strong resistance' and places sell orders. Smart Money then sweeps these levels, collecting all the pending orders (buy stops, sell stops, stop losses, breakevens) and moves in the opposite direction. Pattern-based traders (bull flag, bearish flag, channel breakout) are particularly vulnerable to engineered liquidity traps.
key_rules: Engineered Liquidity = trap designed by Smart Money for retail support/resistance traders
Equal lows (double/triple bottom) = engineered liquidity (NOT real support)
Equal highs (double/triple top) = engineered liquidity (NOT real resistance)
Retail pattern traders (bull flag, bearish flag, channels) are prime targets
Smart Money creates these patterns to accumulate pending orders at those levels
Then sweeps the engineered liquidity → collects stops/breakevens → moves opposite direction
Smart Money traders NEVER consider retail support and resistance as valid levels
Engineered liquidity understanding is essential for valid/fake CHoCH (next lecture)

engineered_liquidity_real_chart.llm_summary: The presenter demonstrates engineered liquidity on a real forex chart. Multiple instances are identified: (1) Equal lows at the same level — retail sees 'support', Smart Money sees engineered liquidity to sweep. (2) Equal highs at the same level — retail sees 'resistance', Smart Money sweeps above. (3) The market alternates between sweeping buy-side and sell-side engineered liquidity as it moves. When market needs to move up, it first sweeps sell-side engineered liquidity (below equal lows) to collect sell stops, then reverses upward. When market needs to move down, it sweeps buy-side engineered liquidity (above equal highs) to collect buy stops, then reverses downward. Trendline-based engineered liquidity is also shown: market creates channels and flag patterns that trendline traders trade, then breaks out to hit their stop losses and breakevens, using that liquidity for its real move. The concept is critical for the next lecture on valid vs fake CHoCH.
key_rules: Equal lows on chart = engineered liquidity (sell-side) — Smart Money sweeps below
Equal highs on chart = engineered liquidity (buy-side) — Smart Money sweeps above
Market alternates between sweeping buy-side and sell-side engineered liquidity
Trendline channels and flags are also engineered liquidity traps
Trendline traders get trapped: breakout → reversal → stops hit → real move begins
Market designs liquidity at every level as it moves — later returns to sweep it
This concept directly feeds into valid/fake CHoCH determination (V09)
